prompt.context_jp: 忙しさに紛れて見過ごされがちな小さな溜め息___、その口から漏れた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 忙しさに紛れて見過ごされがちな小さな溜め息___、その口から漏れた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that marks this newly-introduced sigh.

feedback.correct_en: The sigh is new information being introduced to the scene — it hasn't been mentioned before. が marks this fresh subject that 'escaped from her lips.'
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make the sigh an already-established topic, which doesn't fit this narrative-introducing moment. を doesn't work because the sigh is the subject of 漏れた (intransitive), not an object.

contrast_examples.jp: その溜め息は深かった。

prompt.context_jp: 朝のＳ＆Ｆ本社___、いつもより湿った空気に包まれていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 朝のＳ＆Ｆ本社___、いつもより湿った空気に包まれていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that sets the scene topic.

feedback.correct_en: The S&F headquarters is being set up as the topic/stage of the chapter's opening. は presents it as 'as for the headquarters this morning...'
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce it as brand-new information competing with other subjects, which clashes with its scene-setting role. に would mark it as a location rather than the subject of 包まれていた.

contrast_examples.en: HQ is on fire! (sudden new info)

prompt.context_jp: 切られるのは 派遣ではありません あなた方 社員___です
prompt.prompt_jp: 切られるの___ 派遣ではありません。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking 'the ones who get cut' as topic under discussion.

feedback.correct_en: '切られるのは' sets up 'the ones to be cut' as the topic, then contrasts派遣 vs 社員. は is used because Omae is framing a known topic and revealing the identity.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would awkwardly present 'the cut ones' as new information rather than the topic under discussion. を doesn't fit — 切られるの is already nominalized as subject.

contrast_examples.en: The one chosen is him. (topic frame)

prompt.context_jp: 彼女の辞書___ "不可能"と"残業"の文字はない
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼女の辞書___ "不可能"と"残業"の文字はない
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle framing 'her dictionary' as the setting/topic.

feedback.correct_en: に marks 'her dictionary' as the location/domain where those words don't exist. This is the classic 〜に〜はない existence pattern.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would try to make the dictionary the subject, but ない requires the location marker. を doesn't fit existence predicates.

contrast_examples.jp: 冷蔵庫にビールはない。
contrast_examples.en: There's no beer in the fridge.

prompt.context_jp: ＡＩという新しい存在をどう味方につけるか___、話題の中心にあった。
prompt.prompt_jp: ＡＩという新しい存在をどう味方につけるか___、話題の中心にあった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle identifying THIS specific question as the center of discussion.

feedback.correct_en: が exhaustively identifies what the center of the discussion is — specifically 'how to make AI an ally,' not something else.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would merely topicalize and lose the 'this one specifically' focus. に would mark a location/target, not a subject identity.

prompt.context_jp: ＡＩ___ あなたが思っているより 優秀です
prompt.prompt_jp: ＡＩ___ あなたが思っているより 優秀です
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that makes AI the topic being commented on.

feedback.correct_en: Omae is making a general statement about AI as the topic: 'As for AI, it's more capable than you think.' は is standard for such generic topic comments.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would awkwardly single out AI as new/contrastive info in a generic statement. を doesn't fit with a copula predicate.

prompt.context_jp: 私の ひとを見る目___ ＡＩよりも優れています
prompt.prompt_jp: 私の ひとを見る目___ ＡＩよりも優れています
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that contrasts Omae's judgment against AI's.

feedback.correct_en: は carries a contrastive emphasis here: 'my eye for people (as opposed to other things/AI's judgment) is superior.' It also sets 'my eye for people' as the topic being evaluated.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would exhaustively identify, which clashes with the comparative statement structure (〜よりも優れている). も would mean 'also,' changing meaning.

contrast_examples.en: He CAN speak English (implying other things he can't).
HE is the one who speaks English.

prompt.context_jp: 派遣社員たちの手___一瞬止まり、フロアの空気が張り詰めた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 派遣社員たちの手___一瞬止まり、フロアの空気が張り詰めた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking the sudden event-subject.

feedback.correct_en: The temp workers' hands stopping is a sudden, observable new event — classic が territory for perceived/witnessed happenings.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make it a topic-comment, losing the immediacy of 'their hands froze.' を doesn't fit with intransitive 止まる.

contrast_examples.en: As for the clock, it's running.

prompt.context_jp: 課長になっても やっぱり あなた___甘ちゃんです
prompt.prompt_jp: やっぱり あなた___甘ちゃんです
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle framing 'you' as the topic Omae is commenting on.

feedback.correct_en: Omae makes a judgment about Satonaka as the topic: 'as for you, you're still a softie.' は fits personal evaluation comments.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would identify him exclusively ('YOU are the softie'), which sounds accusatory/exhaustive and misses Omae's reflective, knowing tone. を doesn't fit the copula.

prompt.context_jp: 東海林課長___、鏡でも見てきたのか妙に機嫌よく現れ、福岡亜紀の前で立ち止まった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 東海林課長___、妙に機嫌よく現れ、福岡亜紀の前で立ち止まった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle introducing Tokairin entering the scene.

feedback.correct_en: Tokairin is entering the narrative as a newly-appearing character/event. が marks this appearance-type verb (現れる) subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would presuppose he's already the topic, but here he's being introduced into the scene as new information. に marks direction/time, not subject.

prompt.context_jp: 亜紀は前髪の先___指でつまんでみせ、控えめに答えた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 亜紀は前髪の先___指でつまんでみせ、控えめに答えた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking what Aki pinched.

feedback.correct_en: つまむ (to pinch) is a transitive verb — the tips of her bangs are its direct object, marked with を.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make the bangs the subject, but Aki is doing the pinching. に would mark location/target, not the object being manipulated.

prompt.context_jp: 課長の口元がにやけるのを、大前は書類の陰___冷ややかに眺めていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 大前は書類の陰___冷ややかに眺めていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking where Omae watched from.

feedback.correct_en: から marks the source/vantage point of her gaze — 'from behind the documents.' Looking FROM a hidden position.
feedback.incorrect_en: で would mark a location of action generally, but 'from behind' specifically needs から. に marks static existence or direction, not source of viewing.

prompt.context_jp: 競合との差別化___必要不可欠です
prompt.prompt_jp: 競合との差別化___必要不可欠です
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle making 'differentiation from competitors' the topic.

feedback.correct_en: Omae makes a generic principle statement about what differentiation is — 'As for differentiation, it's indispensable.' は fits abstract/categorical claims.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would exclusively identify the one indispensable thing among many, which is odd in a standalone declarative. を doesn't fit the copula structure.

contrast_examples.en: EFFORT (as opposed to other things) is what's important.

prompt.context_jp: 遠くのスーパーより 近くのコンビニ___頼りです
prompt.prompt_jp: 遠くのスーパーより 近くのコンビニ___頼りです
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle emphasizing the convenience store (as opposed to the supermarket).

feedback.correct_en: After 〜より comparison, が exhaustively identifies the thing that IS reliable: 'it's the nearby convenience store (not the far supermarket) that they rely on.'
feedback.incorrect_en: は would just topicalize without the identification punch needed after a より comparison. を doesn't fit this predicate ('is a reliance').

contrast_examples.en: Rather than this, THAT one is better.

prompt.context_jp: 焦りと不安に押しつぶされそうな里中の姿___、大前は横目で確かめていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 里中の姿___、大前は横目で確かめていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking what Omae was checking.

feedback.correct_en: 確かめる is transitive — Omae's object of checking is Satonaka's figure. を marks this direct object, fronted for emphasis.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make 里中の姿 the subject of 確かめていた, but Omae is doing the checking. は would make it a contrastive topic but the direct-object reading is cleaner here.

prompt.context_jp: 「ＡＩには 人の心までは ___ない」
prompt.prompt_jp: ＡＩには 人の心までは ___ない
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb that fits 'AI can't ___ people's hearts.'

feedback.correct_en: 読み取る means to read/perceive/decipher subtle meaning — the exact verb for understanding hearts/intentions. Its potential 読み取れる fits 'can't grasp.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 読み出す means to retrieve data from storage — too technical. 読み上げる means to read aloud — doesn't fit perceiving emotions.

contrast_examples.jp: 表情から気持ちを読み取る。

prompt.context_jp: 「___の一手だな」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「___の一手だな」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the idiom meaning 'a last-ditch, life-saving move.'

feedback.correct_en: 起死回生 (kishi-kaisei, 'raising from death') means a dramatic comeback move — exactly what the CEO means about saving the company.
feedback.incorrect_en: 一石二鳥 means 'two birds with one stone' (efficiency, not rescue). 七転八倒 means 'writhing in agony' — opposite of a solution.

contrast_examples.jp: 起死回生のホームラン。

prompt.context_jp: 「勝つために コンビニの企画 ___でやります」
prompt.prompt_jp: コンビニの企画 ___でやります
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the phrase meaning 'with everything I've got, desperately.'

feedback.correct_en: 死に物狂い means 'desperately, fighting as if dying' — the right fixed phrase for giving your all.
feedback.incorrect_en: 死人に口なし is a proverb ('dead men tell no tales') — unrelated. 命がけ知らず isn't a real expression.

contrast_examples.en: To protect at the risk of one's life.

prompt.context_jp: 「俺ね そういうの ___んだよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: そういうの ___んだよ
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the adjective meaning 'sharp-eyed, quick to notice.'

feedback.correct_en: 目ざとい means 'quick to notice, keen-eyed' — Tokairin is bragging about spotting small changes like a haircut.
feedback.incorrect_en: 目まぐるしい means 'dizzying, dazzlingly fast.' 目が高い is a set phrase (not written as one word) meaning 'having good taste/discernment' — a different nuance.

prompt.context_jp: 「派遣の私が 社運を懸けた プロジェクトに物申すなど ___です」
prompt.prompt_jp: 物申すなど ___です
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the expression meaning 'overstepping one's bounds.'

feedback.correct_en: 出過ぎたマネ (deshigita mane) literally 'overstepping behavior' is the set phrase for presumptuous conduct — exactly Omae's self-deprecating business expression.
feedback.incorrect_en: 行き過ぎた道 isn't a set phrase. 過ぎたる者 is archaic and means 'one who excels,' unrelated to overstepping.

contrast_examples.jp: 出過ぎたマネをお許しください。

prompt.context_jp: 「課長になっても やっぱり あなたは___です」
prompt.prompt_jp: やっぱり あなたは___です
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word for 'softie, naive person.'

feedback.correct_en: 甘ちゃん (amachan) is a colloquial word for someone soft-hearted or naive — Omae's fond jab at Satonaka's unchanged softness.
feedback.incorrect_en: 辛ちゃん and 苦ちゃん aren't real words. Only 甘い extends into this colloquial noun form.

prompt.context_jp: 「独自のアイデアを ___くれ ギリギリまで考えるんだ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 独自のアイデアを ___くれ
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb meaning 'squeeze/wring out (ideas).'

feedback.correct_en: 絞り出す means to wring/squeeze out — the standard collocation with アイデア for generating ideas with effort.
feedback.incorrect_en: 引き出す (draw out) is used for drawing out ability/money, less idiomatic with one's own ideas. 吐き出す (spit out) has a negative/venting nuance unfit for business creativity.

prompt.context_jp: 「コンビニに来るのは ___で フラっと 来店できる客ばかりではありません」
prompt.prompt_jp: コンビニに来るのは ___で フラっと 来店できる客
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word meaning 'empty-handed.'

feedback.correct_en: 手ぶら (tebura) means literally 'empty hands' — customers arriving without baggage/kids, able to drop by casually.
feedback.incorrect_en: 手抜き means 'cutting corners / slacking.' 手遅れ means 'too late.' Neither fits the context of arriving at a store.

contrast_examples.jp: 手ぶらで来てください。

prompt.context_jp: 「私は ＡＩではありません ___で考えてください」
prompt.prompt_jp: ___で考えてください
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the expression meaning 'by yourself / on your own.'

feedback.correct_en: 自分で考える is the standard set phrase for 'think for yourself.' Omae's blunt line uses this common form.
feedback.incorrect_en: 自身で is more formal/literary and less natural in casual rebuke. 自体で isn't used this way — 自体 means 'itself' as in a thing's essence.

prompt.context_jp: Satonaka is scolding his subordinate for over-relying on AI data.
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds most natural for a frustrated section chief telling his subordinate to stop relying on AI?

choices.text: ＡＩに頼ってないで やるんだ
ＡＩを頼らずに やってください
ＡＩから頼らないで やっているんだ

feedback.correct_en: The story uses ＡＩに頼る (rely ON AI — に marks the thing relied on) with the imperative-ish 〜んだ ending, capturing Satonaka's firm but familiar tone to his own staff.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is grammatical but overly polite — doesn't match a chief addressing his team. C mangles particles (頼る takes に, not から) and uses the wrong verb form.

prompt.context_jp: Tokairin notices Aki's haircut and comments casually.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds most natural for a boss casually noting a subordinate's haircut?

choices.text: あなたは髪を切りましたか？
君は髪が切られたよね？

feedback.correct_en: The informal 君 + dropped particle + よね tag makes a natural, light observation. This is how a chatty boss opens small talk.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is textbook-polite and sounds like a stranger, not a boss chatting. C uses passive incorrectly — getting your hair cut isn't passive in Japanese, and 君は〜が is awkward.

prompt.context_jp: Omae tells Satonaka that if he wants to change his situation, he himself must change.
prompt.prompt_en: Which form best captures the emphatic 'YOU are the one who must change'?

choices.text: あなたが変わるしかない
あなたは変わるしかない
あなたを変わるしかない

feedback.correct_en: が exhaustively identifies Satonaka as THE one who must change — matches Omae's pointed, cutting delivery. This is the identifying/exhaustive が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would dilute the force into a neutral topic comment. を is ungrammatical — 変わる is intransitive.

contrast_examples.en: YOU are the only one who can do it.
As for you, you have no choice but to do it.

prompt.context_jp: Omae curtly tells the men to stop worrying about hair and get to work.
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds most natural as Omae's blunt command?

choices.text: 髪の毛の心配してる場合ですか？ 仕事しなさい！
髪の毛が心配している場合だと思います。仕事をしましょう。
髪の毛について心配される時でありますね。仕事されてください。

feedback.correct_en: 〜場合ですか？ is a rhetorical scold meaning 'is this the time to be worrying about...?' paired with the sharp imperative 仕事しなさい — perfectly Omae.
feedback.incorrect_en: B flips the meaning (saying it IS the time to worry) and sounds wishy-washy. C mangles keigo (passive 心配される, incorrect 〜されてください) and sounds non-native.

contrast_examples.en: Is this the time to be playing around?!

prompt.context_jp: Omae enters the meeting with documents and expresses her desire for the project to succeed.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds most natural for Omae entering a business meeting room?

choices.text: 失礼いたします。このプロジェクトを成功させたいと思ってます
おじゃまします。このプロジェクトを成功させたいよ
こんにちは。このプロジェクトが成功させたいと思います

feedback.correct_en: 失礼いたします is the standard humble entrance for a workplace meeting. 成功させたい uses the causative-desire structure correctly with を.
feedback.incorrect_en: B's おじゃまします is for visiting someone's home; よ ending is too casual for a meeting. C uses が where を is needed (〜を成功させたい), and こんにちは is wrong for entering a meeting room.

contrast_examples.jp: 失礼いたします。資料をお持ちしました。
contrast_examples.en: Excuse me. I've brought the documents.

contrast_examples.jp: おじゃまします。(訪問先で)
